A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GH-ESD and GESD, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v2 includes Appendices A–D, whereas v3 ends after the references and cites supplementary sections S1–S4 that are not supplied. Appendix-dependent comparisons are therefore incomplete; those references do not establish that the underlying content was deleted.

before.justification: v2 reports original GH-ESD detection and segmentation results, component analyses, and model-repair experiments, including Tables 1, 3–4 and appendix Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and model-repair results in Tables 1–4 and reports additional comparative and ablation outcomes in Sections 5.1–5.2.

M1.justification: The documented core pipeline remains knowledge/data-driven hypothesis construction, grounded VLM matching, and sliding-window slope verification. v2 already reports evaluating Spearman alternatives; v3 specifies a multi-scale version and its thresholds without establishing a change to the existing algorithm. The default slope-based procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain GESD detection and segmentation using COCO, KITTI and face-detection data; Waterbirds, CelebA and NICO++ bias discovery; and detection/classification repair. NICO++ correlation settings remain 75%, 90% and 95%. The added comparisons concern existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a separately evaluated HiBug2 variant using Gemini-2.5-Pro alongside the GPT-backed HiBug2 comparator. FACTS*, HiBug*, and the comparator sets in the classification discovery and repair tables remain unchanged. This is a limited expansion through an additional baseline variant.

E3.justification: v2 specifies k=10 for all experiments; v3 makes it the default and additionally evaluates P@5 and P@20. v3 also introduces a matched-Gemini baseline control and KD-only/DD-only evaluations. Its newly disclosed GPT-5.2 baseline implementation does not establish that the corresponding v2 experiments used a different backend.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds an analysis of knowledge-driven versus data-driven hypotheses and their complementarity. Section 5.1 adds an aggregate FP/FN comparison with HiBug2. v3 also reports an FDR-control check and quantifies the Spearman alternative already mentioned in v2. Existing grounding, tag-comparison and threshold-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 explicitly reports a Spearman significance criterion of p<0.05 and stability under Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction, neither documented in v2. Tables 3–4 retain three repair repetitions and ten independent classification-repair runs with the same uncertainty reporting; no increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds P@5/P@20 results, including GH-ESD scores of 0.78/0.66, and Gemini-backed HiBug2 scores of 0.77/0.63/0.52 at k=5/10/20. It reports KD-only/DD-only/joint P@10 of 0.62/0.21/0.73, FP/FN breakdowns, and Spearman F1 of 0.78 versus slope F1 of 0.77. The HiBug2 slice count changes from 3,607 to 3,666. Existing P@10 and Tables 2–4 results remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding; supplementary results cannot be fully compared.

T1.justification: The shared main-text mathematical formulation, matching-score equation and slope statistic are unchanged. However, v2 Appendix C.5 supplies explicit repair-loss and GroupDRO weight-update definitions, while v3 directs readers to unavailable supplementary Section S3.5. Their retention or revision cannot be verified.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: grounded hypothesis-driven instance-level discovery, the GESD benchmark, detection/segmentation applicability, and actionable model repair. The headline P@10 advantage remains 0.73 versus 0.63.

C2.justification: v3 expands the explanation of data-driven hypotheses to include distribution-amplified rare patterns, interprets KD/DD results as complementary, and uses the matched-backend comparison to attribute gains to the framework. The conclusion's limitations concerning dataset coverage and incomplete hypothesis spaces remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Verified edits include disclosure of GPT-5.2 baseline implementations, confidence calibration and Spearman thresholds, addition of a face-dataset URL, and removal of the promise to release GESD upon acceptance. However, v2's prompts, hardware/runtime information and detailed repair settings have unavailable supplementary counterparts in v3. The overall extent of reproducibility-documentation changes cannot be determined.

R1.justification: The same 31 cited works remain. v3 refines VISLIX's description to emphasize expert interaction through ROI exploration and adds an argument that FACTS-style Bayesian correction assumes a stable tag space incompatible with open-ended hypothesis generation. These are limited positioning changes.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammatical and explanatory edits, updates an author's name and affiliations, and fixes the suppressed-title running header. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact. Appendix A–D references become supplementary S1–S4 references, whose contents are unavailable for comparison.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from one P@10 row to three cutoff rows and gains a HiBug2 backend column. Figure 4 is rerendered with minor label cleanup while retaining its examples and trends. Other main figures are retained, and several figures and tables move with text reflow. Supplementary displays cannot be compared.

improvement.justification: The matched-backend control, KD/DD ablation, quantitative Spearman/FDR checks and corrected slice count strengthen the visible main text. However, v3's referenced supplement is unavailable, preventing assessment of the prompts, detailed segmentation evidence, repair formulas and implementation settings supplied in v2. These gaps prevent a reliable paper-level judgment about the net improvement in evidence and technical completeness.
